title: Product management
description: Define the user outcome, evidence for the change and the smallest version worth shipping.
questions: Who faces this problem and what do they do today?
What result would show the change helped them?
Which assumption can the team test before committing to the full scope?

sources.title: Christensen Institute, Jobs to Be Done Theory

specialists.title: Product discovery lead
specialists.focus: Identify the affected user and their progress in a concrete situation. Compare the observed problem with the proposed solution and the workaround users already use.

specialists.title: Product analyst
specialists.focus: Specify the outcome event, eligible population, baseline and decision window. Identify signals that would distinguish adoption from sustained improvement.

specialists.title: Scope and prioritization lead
specialists.focus: Define the smallest complete user flow that could test the main assumption. Identify dependencies, deferred cases and the cost of leaving the current flow in place.

specialists.title: Adoption and rollout lead
specialists.focus: Identify groups whose work changes, what support they need and how the team would pause or reverse rollout if friction rises.

evidence: Recent support tickets, user interviews or workflow observations showing who encountered the problem, under what conditions and what they tried next.
A current baseline for the target outcome, including eligible users or transactions, time window and known data gaps.
Current workflow, dependencies and acceptance examples for the intended path, including one consequential exception or role boundary.
Existing rollout, support and analytics capabilities that the team can use to test or reverse the change.
challenge: Compare leave as is, improve the existing workflow and deliver a small new slice. Explain which user friction each option addresses.
Test the proposed priority against a counterexample such as a less frequent problem with a greater consequence or a group for whom the workaround already succeeds.
Challenge success numbers that rise when usage grows but leave the target problem unchanged. State the data or experiment needed to separate those effects.
Identify a product assumption that could be tested without building the full feature. Explain which result would change the recommendation.
decision_criteria: Recommend a build when observed demand, a complete first slice and a measurable improvement are supported by the evidence.
Recommend discovery or a pilot when affected users are known but the cause, demand or replacement workflow is still uncertain. Name the test and what would count as enough evidence.
Recommend keeping or improving the current workflow when it addresses the verified need with lower support and maintenance cost.
Condition rollout on a named owner, a baseline and an agreed threshold for pausing or revising the release.
